# PRISMA 2020 flow

![PRISMA 2020 flow diagram of the May 2026 update (strict criterion), generated with the PRISMA2020 R package by `R/04_prisma_flow.R`. Title and abstract screening was performed by a staged automated procedure (deterministic keyword rule set, large language model adjudication of abstracts for records without a detected TTP signal, then relevance triage) rather than by two independent human reviewers in Covidence, which was used for de-duplication only. All reports sought for full text were present in the database export, so no separate identification route is shown. Of the 4,605 records screened, 3,254 were unique: a further 1,351 duplicate records that Covidence had not detected were identified after export. A second, inclusive re-screen of the 54 reports excluded only for lacking a quantitative TTP-outcome association identified 40 further studies, which form the sensitivity pool (140 studies in total) and are not shown in the flow.](PRISMA_v4_prisma2020.svg){#fig-prisma width="100%"}

# Search strategy

Records were identified on May 22, 2026, from inception, from five sources:

- **PubMed** (1,250 records)
- **Embase** (2,877)
- **Scopus** (1,649)
- **Web of Science Core Collection** (237)
- **Cochrane CENTRAL** (1)

Combined yield: 6,014 records → 1,409 duplicates removed in Covidence → 4,605 records entered screening. A further 1,351 of those were subsequently identified as duplicate records that Covidence had not detected, so 3,254 of the screened records were unique.

No title and abstract screening was recorded in Covidence, which was used for de-duplication only. Screening was performed by the staged automated procedure described in appendix section 1.8: a deterministic keyword rule set assigned every record to one of five tiers by whether its title and abstract carried a time-to-positivity concept and a bloodstream-infection concept; tier-3 records (blood-culture concept, no detected time-to-positivity signal) with a retrievable PubMed abstract were re-examined by a large language model, which promoted 146 of 299; and records carrying a signal were triaged for relevance, yielding 45 priority candidates. An AI-assisted semantic search tool (Elicit) ranked the same literature in parallel.

Together these routes sent 355 reports to full-text review. Every one of the 355 is present in the database export (333 matched on DOI and the remaining 22 on normalised title), so the semantic search identified no record that the five database searches had not already retrieved. It did, however, do most of the selecting: only 144 of the 355 carried a time-to-positivity signal that the keyword rule set had identified.

| How the record reached full-text review | Reports |
|:---------------------------------------------------------------|--------:|
| Time-to-positivity signal together with a blood-culture concept (tiers 1–2) | 144 |
| Tiered, but no time-to-positivity signal together with a blood-culture concept (tiers 3–5) | 142 |
| Never tiered: matched a study in the earlier review, or flagged for manual checking | 69 |
| **Total sought for full-text review** | **355** |

: The 355 reports sought for full text, by what the keyword rule set had identified in the title and abstract. The 142 tiered without a signal comprise 125 in tier 3, 5 in tier 4 and 12 in tier 5. By retrieval route the same 355 comprise 311 surfaced only by the semantic ranking, 32 only by keyword tiering and relevance triage, and 12 by both. {#tbl-selection-route}

Relevance triage classified only the records promoted at the abstract stage; it did not individually classify the records already in tier 1. It prioritised 45 reports, of which 44 entered the screening pool; the remaining report (growth in anaerobic bottles as a predictor of mortality in *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* bloodstream infection) was dropped without a recorded reason and was not assessed. Of 814 unique records carrying a time-to-positivity signal, 144 reached full-text review and 670 were deferred without an individual eligibility decision. Of those 670, 142 report a clinical outcome; excluding paediatric and neonatal populations leaves 88 that meet the population and outcome criteria on their title and abstract and were never assessed. This is stated as a limitation in the main text.

Because tiering used whatever title and abstract each record carried, duplicate records of the same report could be tiered differently; a report is treated here as carrying a signal if any of its records did, which makes 814 unique reports across tiers 1 and 2.

CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, medRxiv, bioRxiv, forward citation tracking, and reference-list searching were specified in the protocol but not carried out for the update. The 57 baseline studies came from an earlier (thesis) review; two of them were found by hand-searching.

The search strings are in the supplementary appendix (section 1).

# Eligibility criteria

## Strict (primary pool, n=100 studies)

A study qualifies if **all** of the following hold:

1. **Population**: adult bacteremia, candidemia, or other bloodstream infection confirmed by blood culture
2. **Exposure**: TTP (time to blood culture positivity) measured by an automated continuous-monitoring system
3. **Outcome**: at least one clinical outcome reported — mortality, persistent bacteremia, microbiological clearance, or relapse
4. **Quantitative TTP↔outcome association**: 2×2 table by TTP category, OR/HR/RR with CI, or β-per-hour with SE

Studies that report TTP and outcomes only descriptively (without a quantitative TTP↔outcome model) are excluded under the strict criterion.

## Inclusive (sensitivity pool, n=140 studies)

Loosens criterion (4): a paper qualifies if TTP and a clinical outcome are both reported in the same cohort, **even if not cross-tabulated**. Inclusive-only studies are flagged with `[INCLUSIVE_ONLY]` in `tbl_study.notes` and are used only in sensitivity analyses.

## Standing exclusions (both pools)

- Narrative review, case report (n<10), editorial, conference abstract only, study protocol
- TTP not measured (e.g., duration-of-bacteremia in days, time-to-antibiotic, transit time)
- TTP used solely as part of a CRBSI case definition (`[CONTAMINATED_TTP]` flag)
- Population not BSI
- Full text not in English and not extractable

# Data extraction

Two-table extraction into the project's master workbook `TTP_MetaAnalysis_Extraction_Complete_v4.xlsx`, with sheets:

- `tbl_study` — study-level (design, country, dates, single/multi-center, funding, 6-domain QUIPS risk of bias)
- `tbl_population` — arm-level demographics, pathogen class/species, infection source, severity, empiric Rx
- `tbl_ttp` — arm-level TTP reporting (continuous/dichotomized/categorical), unit, mean/median/IQR, cutpoint
- `tbl_outcomes` — outcome rows (one or more per arm) — events, totals, effect estimates, adjustment

Independent second-pass QC was performed on the 43 new strict-pool extractions; 7 factual corrections were applied prior to analysis (see `QC_Verification_Report.md`).

# Effect-size computation

Computed in `R/01_prepare_data.R` using `metafor::escalc()`:

| Preference | Method | metafor measure | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | 2×2 events by TTP category | `OR` | `add = 0.5, to = "only0"` zero-cell correction |
| 2nd | Reported effect estimate + 95% CI | back-calc | log(OR/HR/RR); SE = (log(CI_hi) − log(CI_lo)) / 3.92 |
| 3rd | Continuous per-hour | β or log(OR_per_hour) | Kept separate from 2×2/back-calc pool by `es_source` flag |

# Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis

## Model

$$y_i \mid \text{SE}_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu + u_s,\, \text{SE}_i^2), \quad u_s \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$$

## Priors

| Parameter | Prior |
|---|---|
| Pooled log-OR ($\mu$) | $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ |
| Between-study SD ($\tau$) | Half-Cauchy$(0, 0.5)$ |
| Moderator coefficients | $\mathcal{N}(0, 0.5)$ |

## Sampling

`brms` with the Stan backend: 4 chains × 4,000 iterations (1,000 warm-up), `adapt_delta = 0.99`, `max_treedepth = 12`. Convergence assessed by $\hat{R} < 1.01$ and bulk-ESS > 1,000.

## Sensitivity analyses

1. **Inclusive pool** (n=140) added to test robustness to lower-quality studies
2. **Pathogen subgroups** (gram+ / gram−) via meta-regression
3. **TTP cutpoint** as a meta-regression moderator (per-hour log-OR change)
4. **Data source** — 2×2 vs back-calculated vs continuous
5. **Adjustment status** — adjusted vs unadjusted reported estimates
6. **Publication year trend** — per-year log-OR change
